findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime fields
findings.description: The audit-log endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"`, and `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a Django `DateTimeField`. This paginator applies `math.floor` or `math.ceil` directly to that datetime when building response cursors, raising `TypeError` for any nonempty result. Its `value_from_cursor` also fails to convert timestamp cursor values back to datetimes, unlike `DateTimePaginator`. Preserve the datetime conversion contract, preferably by extending the existing datetime paginator. Add tests for a nonempty optimized response and forward/backward cursor navigation.

findings.title: Unconditional membership lookup breaks organization-token requests
findings.description:
`RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is explicitly optional. Organization API credentials can receive organization access without a corresponding user membership, as supported by `from_rpc_auth` in `src/sentry/auth/access.py`. For those requests, accessing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`.

This expression runs even when `optimized_pagination` is absent, so the change also breaks the existing pagination path. Evaluate advanced eligibility only when requested, guard the optional member, and keep valid non-member authentication on the standard path. Add a regression test using organization-scoped credentials.

findings.title: Negative-offset feature passes unsupported slices to Django
findings.description:
Django querysets reject negative slice indexes; they do not automatically handle them as the comment claims. With advanced features enabled, a parsed cursor such as `0:-1:0` reaches `queryset[-1:100]` and raises `ValueError` instead of returning a page. `Cursor.from_string` accepts this offset.

Reject negative offsets with the established `BadPaginationError` mechanism, or implement a supported reverse-query strategy using nonnegative bounds. Cover both cursor directions with negative-offset tests.
